assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Mankind Pharma (consolidated, ₹ crore), as of 30-Sep-2026 on Q1FY27 results. Bharat Serums and Vaccines (BSV) has been consolidated since 23-Oct-2024, so the base year FY26 already holds a full year of BSV revenue, EBITDA, purchase-price amortisation (~₹450 cr a year on ₹8,253 cr of acquired intangibles, not tax-deductible; a deferred-tax credit offsets it in book tax) and acquisition interest. One reportable segment (pharmaceuticals), so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path; the business-line build (domestic prescription business incl. BSV India, consumer healthcare, exports incl. BSV international) sits in `businessLines` and the authoring script checks it sums to model revenue. Net Profit is the attributable figure (MANKIND.patch.js). Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS (the street's majority method: Motilal Oswal, Geojit, HDFC Securities), on EPS before the BSV amortisation so the forecast matches the basis of the multiple's history (see MANKIND.ctx.js); EV/EBITDA (JM Financial's method) and a DCF are cross-checks.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the business-line build below on FY26 revenue of ₹14,278 cr. FY27E ₹15,999 cr (+12.1%): domestic prescription business (ex-consumer) +11% (Q1FY27 +11.0%: chronic +15.8%, acute +10.9%, BSV domestic +17%; management 'double-digit' for FY27; IQVIA secondary +12.7% vs IPM +13.0%), consumer healthcare +7% (Q1 +3.9% after the cash-and-carry channel was shut; guided 'high single digit to double digit' from Q2), exports +20% (Q1 +29%, of which 12-13pp currency; 'high teens' constant-currency guidance for both Mankind and BSV international; the rupee was ~₹95-96 to the dollar in Jul-2026). FY28-29E: domestic +11% / +10.5% (in line with an IPM growing ~10%, chronic share rising toward 50% over 4-5 years), consumer +9% a year, exports +14% / +13% as the currency tailwind fades.

businessLines._why: FY26 by line from the Q4FY26 investor presentation: domestic business ex-consumer healthcare ₹11,338 cr (incl. BSV's India business, ~half of BSV), consumer healthcare ₹879 cr, exports ₹2,061 cr (Mankind exports incl. 48 US products plus BSV international). Growth rates are explained in _revenueWhy.

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (revenue less operating costs, before exceptional items): FY26 25.4% (company adjusted EBITDA 25.4%, reported 24.5% after the ₹130 cr labour-code and other one-off charges), Q1FY27 26.2%. FY27E 26.0% = the middle of management's 25.5-26.5% guidance, reiterated on 30-Jul-2026 even as gross margin is expected to compress from Q2 (West Asia crisis lifting raw-material and freight costs, a weaker rupee); Q1's 72.8% gross margin was helped by low-cost inventory and a weak base. FY28-29E +50bp / +30bp from chronic mix (40% of domestic sales, rising ~1pp a year), BSV's specialty brands growing faster than the base, and employee cost held near 22% of sales (management's stated range). R&D stays at 2.8-3% of sales. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹178 cr of FY28E EBITDA (~₹3.2 of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: Guided at 6-7% of FY27 revenue (Q4FY26 call) as Mankind builds a biotech facility in Vadodara (board approved up to ₹500 cr of investment in Mankind Medicare for it); FY26 ₹737 cr (5.2%), Q1FY27 ₹198 cr. FY27E ₹1,040 cr (6.5%), then ₹1,050 cr and ₹1,000 cr (~5.9% and ~5.1%) as the Vadodara spend peaks and fades. No acquisitions assumed; Rivotril (Roche's clonazepam brand, ~₹20-30 cr of sales) was bought in Q4FY26.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A ₹886 cr = 4.19% of average gross block (₹21,147 cr incl. ₹16,126 cr of intangibles, of which ₹8,253 cr are BSV's acquired brands and relationships). Q1FY27 ₹226 cr (₹904 cr annualised), of which roughly half is BSV acquisition amortisation (CFO, Q1FY27 call). 4.25% gives ₹931 / 975 / 1,018 cr. CWIP (₹655 cr plus ₹473 cr of intangibles under development) is held flat by the engine.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash, which is negative until FY29E (net debt ₹3,932 cr at Mar-26, ₹3,377 cr at Jun-26). Treasury income on the gross cash and liquid-fund balance is built in otherIncome instead.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 30; checked in MANKIND.ctx.js). (1) Treasury income: FY26 interest ₹58 cr + mutual-fund gains ₹127 cr (₹64 cr unrealised) = ₹185 cr on ~₹2,500 cr of average cash, deposits and liquid funds (~7.4%). We apply 6.25% to average gross cash on our path: ₹2,272 cr at Mar-26 (company), ~₹1,560 cr at Mar-27 after repaying ₹2,500 cr of NCDs, ~₹1,320 cr at Mar-28 after the last ₹2,500 cr, ~₹4,190 cr at Mar-29 = ₹120 / 90 / 172 cr. (2) Government grants and export incentives ₹60 cr (FY26 ₹61 cr, FY25 ₹88 cr). (3) Scrap, liabilities written back, insurance and miscellaneous ₹35 cr (FY26 ₹42 cr). (4) Share of associates ₹12 cr (FY26 ₹11.7 cr; Screener counts it in other income). Not forecast: foreign-exchange gains (FY26 ₹70 cr, FY25 ₹20 cr). Excluded as one-offs: exceptional items (FY26 −₹130 cr) and the FY25 ₹164 cr gain on selling Mahananda Spa & Resorts. Total ₹227 / 198 / 280 cr vs FY26 ₹370 cr before exceptional items, ₹336 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 and ₹49 cr in Q1FY27 (lower cash after the Apr-2026 NCD repayment).
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest on borrowings (₹5,000 cr acquisition NCDs at 7.97-7.99%, working-capital lines, related-party loans) and leases
assumptions._interestWhy: Built from the debt schedule (AR FY26 note 22; checked in MANKIND.ctx.js). NCDs: ₹1,250 cr at 7.99% repaid 16-Apr-2026 (15 days in FY27), ₹1,250 cr at 7.99% due 16-Oct-2026 (198 days), ₹2,500 cr at 7.97% due 16-Nov-2027 (full FY27, 229 days of FY28) = ₹258 / 125 / 0 cr; plus 7.5% on ₹1,204 cr of other borrowings (working-capital loans ₹639 cr, related-party loans ₹339 cr, term loans and accrued interest; held flat) = ₹90 cr; leases ~₹10 cr; other finance costs ~₹10 cr. Total ₹368 / 235 / 110 cr. Q1FY27 actual ₹110 cr (₹142 cr in Q4FY26) after the Apr-2026 repayment; FY26 ₹639 cr. We assume the NCDs are repaid from cash, not refinanced (management: acquisition debt repaid by FY28).
assumptions._taxWhy: Q1FY27 25.4% (25.5% per brokers): Mankind moved to the new tax regime (25.17%) in FY27 after the income-tax exemption on its Sikkim plant expired; FY26 was 16.9% and FY25 20.3%. The BSV amortisation is not tax-deductible, but the deferred tax liability created on the acquisition (₹1,800 cr) unwinds at 25.17% of it, so book tax stays near the statutory rate. This is the single biggest drag on FY27E EPS growth (~₹4.5 a share vs FY26's rate).
assumptions._payoutWhy: Mankind paid its first dividend in FY26: an interim ₹1 a share (₹41.27 cr, 2.2% of profit). Cash goes first to repaying the acquisition NCDs (₹1,250 cr in Apr-2026, ₹1,250 cr in Oct-2026, ₹2,500 cr in Nov-2027). We assume a 3% payout (₹1.7-2.4 a share).

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity: 6.5% + 0.8 x 6% = 11.3%. Net debt is ~3% of capital (₹3,377 cr at Jun-26 against a ~₹1.03 lakh cr market value) and falls to nil by FY28, so WACC ≈ cost of equity; beta 0.8 for a defensive, domestic-led pharma company.
dcf._tgWhy: 6% nominal: ~85% of revenue is India, where the branded market grows 8-10% a year in value.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~11% to 8% by year 15.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 27%: a little above the FY29E 26.8% as chronic and specialty mix rise, below the 28-29% of the best Indian branded peers (Abbott, Torrent's base).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: 4.5% of revenue: maintenance plus capacity for 8% growth after the Vadodara build (FY24-26: 3.8-5.2%).
dcf._depWhy: 3% of revenue = tax-deductible depreciation and amortisation only (book D&A FY27E ~5.8% of revenue, of which ~2.8pp is BSV acquisition amortisation that gives no tax saving).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The acute recovery and new divisions take domestic growth back to 1.2x the market, BSV's fertility and Anti-D brands keep compounding at 20%+, consumer healthcare returns to double digits, and gross margin holds above 72%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Mankind stays a market-grower in acute (60% of sales) while GLP-1s and trade generics take share, the Anti-D patent (India, to 2028) invites competition, raw-material costs squeeze gross margin, and exports lose the currency tailwind.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Mankind: three of the four notes standing on 30-Sep-2026 that disclose a method use P/E (Motilal Oswal 40x 12-month-forward EPS, Geojit 37x FY28E, HDFC Securities 34x Q2FY28E; JM Financial uses EV/EBITDA). 43x Sep-28E EPS BEFORE the BSV acquisition amortisation (~₹450 cr a year, ~₹8.2 a share after its deferred-tax credit) and after minorities, because Mankind's short P/E history mixes years with no, partial and full amortisation (handled as in our Torrent report): Mankind's median one-year-forward P/E since 1-Nov-2023 (listed May-2023; IPO months skipped; every weekly close) on EPS before exceptional items and the BSV amortisation, 38.8x, x 1.110 (nine pharma peers' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their medians over the same window: +11.0%, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +11.0%) = 43.1x, nearest half-turn 43x. The engine values reported EPS, so the multiple here is the equivalent on reported Sep-28E EPS (43 x adjusted ÷ reported = 47.31x; bull 46.5x and bear 38.5x adjusted = the 75th/25th percentiles x 1.110, translated the same way). Checked in MANKIND.ctx.js; written by MANKIND.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check (JM Financial's method; neutral to the amortisation). Mankind's median trailing EV/EBITDA since 1-Nov-2023 excluding the BSV transition (23-Oct-2024 to 30-Sep-2025, when EV carried all the deal debt but trailing EBITDA held less than four quarters of BSV) is 29.3x (30.2x with it); x 1.0588 (the peers' EV/EBITDA move against their medians over the same window) = 31.0x, applied to trailing EBITDA at the target date (half FY27E + half FY28E) less net debt at Sep-27. Bull 34.5x / bear 27.5x = 75th / 25th percentiles x the same factor.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 11.3% (cost of equity ≈ WACC: net debt is small and falls to nil), terminal growth 6%; tax shield only on tax-deductible D&A (BSV amortisation excluded); less net debt at Mar-27.

otherTreasury.label: Offset: net deferred tax (₹1,840 cr liability, mostly on BSV brands, less ₹325 cr of assets) in other liabilities/assets
otherTreasury._why: Engine workaround (MANKIND.patch.js note 3). Screener's Mar-26 other liabilities, which the Excel reads unpatched, include the ₹1,839.98 cr deferred tax liability (₹1,799.87 cr of it created on BSV's acquired intangibles) and other assets include ₹324.70 cr of deferred tax assets; neither is working capital. This entry takes the net ₹1,515.28 cr out of working capital (13.4% of FY26 revenue, close to the company's 52 days) in the engine and the Excel alike; investments are raised by the same amount in the patch, so net debt is unchanged, and CWIP is lowered by it so the balance sheet balances.

cover.headline: India's #1 prescription franchise has de-rated below its own history while pharma re-rated: on the street's P/E method, with EPS put on one basis across the BSV deal, we see {{dcf.upside|chg}}
cover.lead: Mankind is India's 4th-largest drug maker by value (4.7% share), #1 by prescriptions for nine years, 79% of revenue from the domestic prescription market and 40% of that in chronic therapies; it bought Bharat Serums and Vaccines (BSV, women's health, fertility, critical-care biologics) for ₹13,768 cr in Oct-2024 with debt. Q1FY27 revenue rose 13% to ₹4,031 cr (domestic prescriptions +11%, exports +29%), EBITDA 25% and profit to shareholders 30%, with growth back at market pace after a lost FY26. We forecast EPS to shareholders of ₹55.2 / 66.5 / 79.7 for FY27-29E (₹63.4 / 74.6 / 87.8 before ~₹450 cr a year of non-cash BSV amortisation) and net cash by FY28E. Three of the four brokers that disclose a method use **P/E**, and so do we: **43x Sep-28E EPS before the BSV amortisation (₹81.2)**, i.e. Mankind's 38.8x median forward P/E since Nov-2023 on the same basis, lifted 11% for the pharma sector's move over the same window, gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹3,316; DCF ₹1,822. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A franchise that is hard to copy
arguments.p: 15.2% of all prescriptions in India, 84% of doctors writing its brands, 18,500+ reps reaching deeper into small towns than peers, 22 brands above ₹100 cr and consumer brands with 28-84% shares (Manforce, Prega News). It turns ordinary molecules into large brands at low cost; gross margin 71-73%, employee cost ~22% of sales.

arguments.h: Growth is back to market pace; outperformance is the upside
arguments.p: A field-force overhaul cost Mankind its growth premium in FY26 (organic +8.6%). Since then: secondary sales +12.7% in Q1FY27 vs the market's 13.0%, acute back to 10.9%, chronic 15.8%, volume 4.7%. We model 10.5-11% domestic growth (market pace); management's aspiration of beating the market again is our bull case, not our base.

arguments.h: BSV: the right asset, a full price, now de-risked financially
arguments.p: ~28x EBITDA for the only recombinant Anti-D, a fertility portfolio and an emerging-market biologics business. Growth recovered to 21% in Q1FY27 (domestic ~17%, international ~25%), but Mankind no longer discloses BSV's numbers. Net debt fell from ₹5,784 cr to ₹3,377 cr in five quarters (0.9x EBITDA); on our path Mankind is net cash by Mar-28 (₹112 cr).

arguments.h: Valuation: de-rated while the sector re-rated
arguments.p: At ₹2,504 the stock trades at 33.6x our FY28E EPS before the BSV amortisation (37.3x reported) against a 38.8x median since Nov-2023 (44.2x on reported EPS); its trailing P/E is −4% vs its own median while pharma peers are +11%. The street (34-40x reported EPS) assumes the de-rating lasts; even on the post-Oct-2025 median (33.2x) the value is above today's price. The DCF (₹1,822) is the warning: the price, like the sector's, rests on the multiple.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): gross margin after higher West Asia-linked input costs, consumer healthcare's return to high-single-digit growth, BSV growth and the domestic business vs the market.

sections.title: India's #4 drug maker by value and #1 by prescriptions: a mass-market brand machine adding chronic, specialty and consumer arms

blocks.p: Mankind sells branded generic medicines in India. It is the 4th-largest company in the Indian pharmaceutical market (IPM) by value with a 4.7% share, 2nd by volume (6.1%), and has had the most prescriptions written for its brands for nine years running (15.2% of all prescriptions in Q1FY27). It built that position the unusual way: low-priced, high-volume brands for common acute conditions (antibiotics, antacids, vitamins, pain), sold by one of India's largest field forces (18,500+ including managers, covering 5 lakh+ doctors) and with a deeper reach into smaller towns than its peers. On top of that base it has added four layers: chronic therapies (cardiac, diabetes, respiratory; 40% of domestic sales ex-BSV), in-licensed specialty products from multinationals (AstraZeneca's Symbicort, Novartis' inclisiran as Crenzlo, Takeda's vonoprazan as Vonalong, Roche's Rivotril), a consumer-healthcare business built on household brands (Manforce condoms, Prega News pregnancy kits, Gas-O-Fast antacid), and since Oct-2024 Bharat Serums and Vaccines (BSV), a maker of complex biologics for women's health, fertility and critical care. Exports (14% of revenue) are mostly BSV's emerging-market business plus 49 US generic launches.

sections.title: From a 1995 start-up to a ₹1 lakh crore company: the IPO, the private-equity exit and the BSV bet

blocks.p: Co-founders Ramesh and Rajeev Juneja started Mankind in 1995 with a focus on affordable brands for general practitioners in smaller towns. Brands such as Manforce and Prega News (2007-10) took it into consumer health; the push into chronic therapies (2018-19) and specialty (Panacea Biotec's brands, FY22; in-licensing from AstraZeneca, Novartis, Takeda and Roche) followed. ChrysCapital and Capital Group were long-time private-equity investors. The May-2023 IPO at ₹1,080 was entirely an offer for sale (4.0 cr shares, ~₹4,326 cr): the company raised nothing. The private-equity funds then sold the rest of their stakes in block deals (Dec-2023 to Jul-2024), and the promoters sold 1.62% in Feb-2024 to meet the 25% public-shareholding rule.

sections.title: The Indian drug market: ₹2.57 lakh crore growing ~10%, tilting to chronic and specialty, with a GLP-1 price war under way

blocks.p: India's domestic formulations market was worth ₹2,565 bn (₹2.57 lakh cr) at the chemist level in FY26, up 9.9% (IQVIA). Growth comes from three parts that move differently: price (4-5% a year; scheduled drugs follow the WPI-linked price-control formula, others may rise up to 10%), new products (~3-4% of sales a year) and volume (low single digits). The mix is shifting toward chronic therapies (cardiac, diabetes, respiratory, CNS) as lifestyle diseases and diagnosis rates rise, and toward specialty and biologics. Two forces stand out in 2026: (1) semaglutide's patent expired in Mar-2026 and 20+ companies launched 35-40 brands, adding to market growth while prices collapse, and (2) trade generics and e-pharmacies keep pressing on prices of older acute molecules, Mankind's heartland. The market grew 10.7% in Q4FY26 (excluding the GLP-1 innovator) and 13.0% in Q1FY27 (excluding tirzepatide).

bullets: **Chronic is where the growth is.** Mankind outgrew the market by 1.25x in chronic over FY21-26 and by 1.55x in cardiac; it lags in gastro and vitamins, two acute categories where it is large.

**GLP-1s.** Mankind deliberately stayed out of the first wave of semaglutide launches ("let this storm pass"; it launched an in-licensed pen in Apr-May 2026 through its diabetes and gynaec divisions, without price cuts). That protects margins but costs share in the fastest-growing molecule; the market-growth figures it quotes exclude tirzepatide.
**Price controls.** FY26 price growth was 4.2% for Mankind vs 4.4% for the market (IQVIA); a large NLEM share in acute caps pricing.
**Consumer health.** Modern trade and e-commerce are taking share from general trade; Mankind's share of OTC sales through them rose from 9% (FY25) to 15% (Q1FY27).

blocks.callout: **So what:** the market Mankind serves grows ~10% a year in value with little cyclicality. Its value is in chronic and specialty; Mankind is a top-5 player in most chronic segments but is still 60% acute, so its growth depends on whether the acute recovery of the last four quarters holds.

sections.title: Does the market's growth reach Mankind? In chronic and BSV, yes; in acute, only at market pace since FY25

blocks.p: For years Mankind grew 1.3-1.7x the market (management). That ended in FY25-26: an enforced overhaul of the field force (high attrition, people removed and replaced about 18 months before Jul-2026) hit acute sales, where relationships with general practitioners matter most. Secondary sales grew only 6.3% in Q2FY26 (acute 3.3%), against a market growing ~10%; organic domestic growth excluding consumer was 8.6% for FY26. The recovery since is real: secondary sales +8.7% in Q4FY26 and +12.7% in Q1FY27 (market +13.0%), acute back to 10.9%, volume growth 4.7% (2.3% in FY26, 0.5% in FY25), field-force productivity ₹7.2 lakh a month per rep in FY26 (₹6.5 lakh in FY25), attrition "back to normal".

sections.title: India prescriptions (79% of revenue): #1 in prescriptions, #4 by value, 40% chronic, and growing with the market again after a lost year

blocks.p: The domestic prescription business (₹11,338 cr in FY26, including BSV's India sales) is Mankind. It rests on scale in the doctor's office: 15.2% of all prescriptions in India (#1 for nine years), 84% of prescribers writing at least one Mankind brand, 13 brands above ₹200 cr and 54 above ₹50 cr. The portfolio is still 60% acute: antibiotics, gastro, vitamins, gynaecology, pain. Chronic therapies are 40% (ex-BSV) after rising from 28% in FY18, led by cardiac (Telmikind family ₹750 cr+, Lipirose and Statpure growing 23-31%) and diabetes (Glizid ₹230 cr+, gliflozins, insulin glargine). Two facts surprise people: Mankind's reach into Tier II-VI towns and villages is 47% of sales against 34% for the market (company), yet the share of its sales from metros and Class-1 towns has risen from 50.7% (FY17) to 56.5% (FY26) as it adds specialists, hospitals and chronic brands. FY26 was weak (organic growth ex-consumer 8.6%) because Mankind rebuilt its field force; Q1FY27 was +11.0% with chronic +15.8% and acute +10.9%.

bullets: **What went wrong in FY26.** Management "did deep correction" of the field force ~18 months before Jul-2026: high attrition, people removed, new divisions formed. Acute growth fell to 3.3% in Q2FY26; secondary sales grew 6.3% vs ~10% for the market.

**What has improved.** Gastro from −2.5% (Q2FY26) to +13.6% (Q1FY27); vitamins from 5% to 19.3%; gynaec from 6.9% to 12.7%; cardiac from 14.5% to 19.4%. Volume growth 4.7% (2.3% in FY26). Attrition and vacancies "back to normal".

**Levers named by management:** chronic toward 50% of sales in 4-5 years; hospitals (share "significantly below peers"); a new division (Vistar) for under-promoted brands; under-penetrated states where its rank is below its national #4.
**What still lags:** new introductions (2.8% of sales vs 4.1% for the market), anti-infectives (+3.6%), and GLP-1s, where Mankind is a late, small player by choice.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** a top-tier franchise that has lost its growth premium. We forecast domestic prescription growth of 11% in FY27E (Q1: 11.0%) and 10.5-11% after, in line with the market; a return to 1.2x the market (management's aspiration) is our bull case.

sections.title: BSV: hard-to-copy biologics in fertility, pregnancy and critical care; growth recovered to 21%, but Mankind no longer discloses its numbers

blocks.p: BSV makes biologics that few companies can: the world's only recombinant Anti-D (given to Rh-negative mothers to protect later pregnancies; 5-7% of Indian mothers, 80 lakh to 1 crore a year, with only 30-40% treated; patent in India until 2028 and, per management, 100% of the Indian market), India's first biosimilar recombinant FSH (Foligraf, for IVF), urinary hormones (Humog, HUCOG), immunoglobulins (IVIG, India's only anti-thymocyte globulin, anti-snake-venom and rabies immunoglobulins) and complex injectables (liposomal amphotericin B, leuprolide microspheres). It makes them at Ambernath (recombinant, equine, hormonal) and in Germany (USFDA-accredited, with its own enzyme and hormone APIs). In FY24 it had revenue of ₹1,723 cr (54% India) and a 28.4% adjusted EBITDA margin, above Mankind's 24.7%. Since the deal BSV has been run as a separate, professionally managed unit; its generic women's-health business moved into Mankind on 1-Nov-2025.

sections.title: Consumer healthcare (6%): category-leading brands, ~5% growth for two years

blocks.p: Mankind's over-the-counter business sells brands most Indians know: Manforce condoms (#1, 28% share), Prega News pregnancy kits (#1, 84%), an emergency contraceptive (#1, 68%), Gas-O-Fast antacid powder (#2, 12%), an anti-acne brand (#1, 34%) and a vitamin brand (#8, 2.3%) (IQVIA retail MAT Jun-2026). Revenue grew from ₹692 cr (FY23) to ₹879 cr (FY26), 8% a year, at an ~18-20% EBITDA margin. Growth slowed in FY26-Q1FY27: a GST change hurt Q2FY26, and Mankind stopped selling to "cash and carry" wholesalers who were undercutting its own general-trade distributors. Modern trade and e-commerce grew 38% in Q1FY27 and are now 15% of consumer sales.

blocks.p: The moat is distribution and doctor relationships: any company can make amoxicillin-clavulanate, but few can sell ₹408 cr of it under one brand. That moat protects market share, not prices, and it showed its limits in FY26 when an internal overhaul cost Mankind its growth premium for a year. BSV adds a genuine technology moat in a few biologics, but at ~13% of revenue it does not yet change the character of the company.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** narrow moat. Mankind deserves a premium to the generic-export pharma names for its domestic franchise and balance-sheet recovery, but not the multiple of a company with proprietary products; its returns on capital (12-14% after the deal) are the honest measure of what the moat earns today.

blocks.p: Mankind's revenue grew from ₹5,865 cr in FY20 to ₹14,278 cr in FY26 (16% a year), with two step-ups: the domestic franchise compounding at ~12-13% and, from 23-Oct-2024, Bharat Serums and Vaccines (BSV, ~13% of revenue). EBITDA margin has barely moved: 24.5% in FY20, 21.7% in FY23 (raw-material inflation and price controls), 25.4% in FY26, because Mankind reinvests scale in its field force and brands. **Profit is where the deal shows.** FY24 profit to shareholders was ₹1,913 cr (EPS ₹47.75); FY26 was the same ₹1,913 cr (EPS ₹46.34) on 3% more shares, as the deal added ~₹450 cr a year of non-cash amortisation, finance cost jumped from ₹34 cr to ₹639 cr and other income fell when ₹13,768 cr of cash and debt went to the sellers. Before exceptional items and the BSV amortisation, FY26 EPS was ₹57.0, up 26% on FY24's ₹45.1.

sections.title: One big bet: ₹13,768 cr for BSV at ~28x EBITDA, funded with debt, a QIP and an asset sale; returns fell from ~26% to 14%

blocks.p: Until 2024 Mankind was a cash machine with a clean balance sheet: net cash of ~₹3,070 cr at Mar-24 (Screener basis), modest capex (₹390-830 cr a year), no dividends, and one bolt-on (Panacea Biotec's specialty brands, FY22). BSV changed that. Mankind paid ₹13,768 cr (enterprise value ₹13,630 cr at signing on 25-Jul-2024, completed 23-Oct-2024) for a business with FY24 revenue of ₹1,723 cr and adjusted EBITDA of ₹489 cr: ~28x EBITDA, a little below the ~30x trailing EV/EBITDA at which Mankind itself traded at the time (Screener). It funded the deal with ₹5,000 cr of NCDs and up to ₹5,000 cr of commercial paper, then retired debt with a ₹3,000 cr QIP (Dec-2024, 1.19 cr shares at ₹2,520, +3% dilution) and ₹562 cr from selling Mahananda Spa & Resorts to Chalet Hotels (Feb-2025). Of the price, ₹6,473 cr (47%) is goodwill and ₹8,253 cr finite-life intangibles.

blocks.callout: **The BSV arithmetic.** At ~28x FY24 EBITDA the deal earns an EBITDA yield of ~3.6% on its price before synergies, against ~8% pre-tax on the NCDs that funded it, and the amortisation (~₹450 cr a year) is not tax-deductible. It creates value only if BSV's specialty brands compound at high teens for years (Q1FY27: +21%) and Mankind's reach lifts BSV's margin. Management has not quantified synergies; HDFC Securities flagged them as delayed in Feb-2026. The company's "ROCE excluding the acquisition" (41%) shows the base business is excellent; the reported 12% shows what shareholders actually earn on the capital now employed.

sections.title: Earnings quality: good cash conversion; read the BSV amortisation, the tax step-up and the tax dispute carefully

bullets: **Acquisition amortisation.** BSV's ₹8,253 cr of intangibles are amortised at ~₹450 cr a year (our estimate from the Q1FY27 call; group intangible amortisation ₹162 cr FY24, ₹362 cr FY25, ₹594 cr FY26). It is not tax-deductible; the ₹1,800 cr deferred tax liability unwinds by ~₹113 cr a year, so it costs ~₹337 cr of reported profit (₹8.2 a share) and no cash.

**Exceptional items.** FY26: −₹129.75 cr (labour-code gratuity and leave ₹97 cr, a trademark assignment between Mankind and BSV, a ₹13 cr BSV project write-down). FY25: +₹164 cr gain on selling Mahananda Spa & Resorts, booked in other income. Screener tags both as exceptional; we exclude both from the earnings history.
**Other income.** ₹359 cr in FY26 included ₹127 cr of mutual-fund gains (₹64 cr unrealised) and ₹70 cr of foreign-exchange gains; Q1FY27 fell to ₹49 cr as cash went to repay debt.
**Tax.** 16.9% in FY26 and ~25% from FY27 (Sikkim plant's exemption ended): reported EPS growth in FY27 is ~9 points lower than pre-tax growth.

**"Cash EPS".** The company adds back all depreciation and amortisation (₹19.2 in Q1FY27), not only acquisition amortisation; Macquarie challenged this on the Q1FY27 call. We use EPS before the BSV amortisation only.
**Cash conversion.** Operating cash flow was 84% / 80% / 89% of company EBITDA in FY24-26 (77% in Q1FY27); capex 3.8-5.2% of revenue. Working capital 52 days.

**Income-tax dispute.** After a search in FY24 the department made adjustments of ₹1,909 cr (₹1,609 cr of expenses disallowed under section 37(1), ₹257 cr of tax-holiday deductions); demands of ₹1,113 cr are contingent liabilities (₹229 cr paid under protest) and the auditors drew attention to it. Section 37(1) disallows expenses incurred for purposes prohibited by law; the filings do not say which expenses were challenged.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing aggressive in revenue or cost recognition, and cash conversion is good. But four things distort reported EPS (non-deductible amortisation for many years, one-off gains and charges, a tax-rate step-up, a large tax dispute) and BSV is no longer disclosed separately. We show reported EPS, EPS to shareholders and EPS before the BSV amortisation side by side.

blocks.p: Mankind is run by its founders and their families: Ramesh Juneja (Chairman), Rajeev Juneja (Vice Chairman and MD), Sheetal Arora (CEO and Whole-time Director, promoter) and Arjun Juneja (COO). sections.title: Valuation: 43x Sep-28E EPS before the BSV amortisation gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}

blocks.p: Of the notes standing on 30-Sep-2026 that disclose a method, three value Mankind on **P/E** (Motilal Oswal 40x 12-month-forward EPS, Geojit 37x FY28E, HDFC Securities 34x Q2FY28E) and one on **EV/EBITDA** (JM Financial 22x Jun-28E). We follow the majority: **P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E)**, the EPS a buyer will look at one year from now. The deal makes one adjustment necessary. BSV added ~₹450 cr a year of non-cash amortisation (₹8.2 a share after its deferred-tax credit) from 23-Oct-2024, so reported EPS in Mankind's short history mixes years with none, 160 days and a full year of it, while the market priced the pre-deal months (Nov-2023 to Jul-2024) on standalone earnings. As in our Torrent Pharma report, we put the history and the forecasts on one basis: **EPS before the BSV amortisation and before exceptional items, after minorities**. EV/EBITDA (JM's method, neutral to the amortisation) and a DCF are cross-checks.

Mankind listed on 9-May-2023, so there is no five-year history. Following the batch rule (PLAYBOOK §7c), we use its own one-year-forward P/E **since 1-Nov-2023**, skipping the IPO months, on every weekly close plus the 30-Sep-2026 close (153 points): price ÷ the next full fiscal year's EPS, actual FY25-26 and our FY27-28E. We multiply the median by the nine-peer pharma factor measured over the **same window** (+11%) and round to the nearest half-turn. No own de-rating, growth or returns adjustment enters the base; those are sensitivities below.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good franchise at a fair-to-cheap price on its own history; the debate is whether growth returns to market-plus

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's #1 prescription franchise and #4 drug maker, 40% chronic and rising, consumer brands that lead their categories, and BSV's biologics; a balance sheet that will be net cash by FY28E; and management with a 30-year record. **What you are not buying:** a pipeline, pricing power, or a company growing faster than its market today.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Mankind Pharma (consolidated, ₹ crore), as of 30-Sep-2026 on Q1FY27 results. Bharat Serums and Vaccines (BSV) has been consolidated since 23-Oct-2024, so the base year FY26 already holds a full year of BSV revenue, EBITDA, purchase-price amortisation (~₹450 cr a year on ₹8,253 cr of acquired intangibles, not tax-deductible; a deferred-tax credit offsets it in book tax) and acquisition interest. One reportable segment (pharmaceuticals), so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path; the business-line build (domestic prescription business incl. BSV India, consumer healthcare, exports incl. BSV international) sits in `businessLines` and the authoring script checks it sums to model revenue. Net Profit is the attributable figure (MANKIND.patch.js). Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS (the street's majority method: Motilal Oswal, Geojit, HDFC Securities), on EPS before the BSV amortisation so the forecast matches the basis of the multiple's history (see MANKIND.ctx.js); EV/EBITDA (JM Financial's method) and a DCF are cross-checks.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the business-line build below on FY26 revenue of ₹14,278 cr. FY27E ₹15,999 cr (+12.1%): domestic prescription business (ex-consumer) +11% (Q1FY27 +11.0%: chronic +15.8%, acute +10.9%, BSV domestic +17%; management 'double-digit' for FY27; IQVIA secondary +12.7% vs IPM +13.0%), consumer healthcare +7% (Q1 +3.9% after the cash-and-carry channel was shut; guided 'high single digit to double digit' from Q2), exports +20% (Q1 +29%, of which 12-13pp currency; 'high teens' constant-currency guidance for both Mankind and BSV international; the rupee was ~₹95-96 to the dollar in Jul-2026). FY28-29E: domestic +11% / +10.5% (in line with an IPM growing ~10%, chronic share rising toward 50% over 4-5 years), consumer +9% a year, exports +14% / +13% as the currency tailwind fades.

businessLines._why: FY26 by line from the Q4FY26 investor presentation: domestic business ex-consumer healthcare ₹11,338 cr (incl. BSV's India business, ~half of BSV), consumer healthcare ₹879 cr, exports ₹2,061 cr (Mankind exports incl. 48 US products plus BSV international). Growth rates are explained in _revenueWhy.

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (revenue less operating costs, before exceptional items): FY26 25.4% (company adjusted EBITDA 25.4%, reported 24.5% after the ₹130 cr labour-code and other one-off charges), Q1FY27 26.2%. FY27E 26.0% = the middle of management's 25.5-26.5% guidance, reiterated on 30-Jul-2026 even as gross margin is expected to compress from Q2 (West Asia crisis lifting raw-material and freight costs, a weaker rupee); Q1's 72.8% gross margin was helped by low-cost inventory and a weak base. FY28-29E +50bp / +30bp from chronic mix (40% of domestic sales, rising ~1pp a year), BSV's specialty brands growing faster than the base, and employee cost held near 22% of sales (management's stated range). R&D stays at 2.8-3% of sales. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹178 cr of FY28E EBITDA (~₹3.2 of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: Guided at 6-7% of FY27 revenue (Q4FY26 call) as Mankind builds a biotech facility in Vadodara (board approved up to ₹500 cr of investment in Mankind Medicare for it); FY26 ₹737 cr (5.2%), Q1FY27 ₹198 cr. FY27E ₹1,040 cr (6.5%), then ₹1,050 cr and ₹1,000 cr (~5.9% and ~5.1%) as the Vadodara spend peaks and fades. No acquisitions assumed; Rivotril (Roche's clonazepam brand, ~₹20-30 cr of sales) was bought in Q4FY26.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A ₹886 cr = 4.19% of average gross block (₹21,147 cr incl. ₹16,126 cr of intangibles, of which ₹8,253 cr are BSV's acquired brands and relationships). Q1FY27 ₹226 cr (₹904 cr annualised), of which roughly half is BSV acquisition amortisation (CFO, Q1FY27 call). 4.25% gives ₹931 / 975 / 1,018 cr. CWIP (₹655 cr plus ₹473 cr of intangibles under development) is held flat by the engine.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash, which is negative until FY29E (net debt ₹3,932 cr at Mar-26, ₹3,377 cr at Jun-26). Treasury income on the gross cash and liquid-fund balance is built in otherIncome instead.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 30; checked in MANKIND.ctx.js). (1) Treasury income: FY26 interest ₹58 cr + mutual-fund gains ₹127 cr (₹64 cr unrealised) = ₹185 cr on ~₹2,500 cr of average cash, deposits and liquid funds (~7.4%). We apply 6.25% to average gross cash on our path: ₹2,272 cr at Mar-26 (company), ~₹1,560 cr at Mar-27 after repaying ₹2,500 cr of NCDs, ~₹1,320 cr at Mar-28 after the last ₹2,500 cr, ~₹4,190 cr at Mar-29 = ₹120 / 90 / 172 cr. (2) Government grants and export incentives ₹60 cr (FY26 ₹61 cr, FY25 ₹88 cr). (3) Scrap, liabilities written back, insurance and miscellaneous ₹35 cr (FY26 ₹42 cr). (4) Share of associates ₹12 cr (FY26 ₹11.7 cr; Screener counts it in other income). Not forecast: foreign-exchange gains (FY26 ₹70 cr, FY25 ₹20 cr). Excluded as one-offs: exceptional items (FY26 −₹130 cr) and the FY25 ₹164 cr gain on selling Mahananda Spa & Resorts. Total ₹227 / 198 / 280 cr vs FY26 ₹370 cr before exceptional items, ₹336 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 and ₹49 cr in Q1FY27 (lower cash after the Apr-2026 NCD repayment).
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest on borrowings (₹5,000 cr acquisition NCDs at 7.97-7.99%, working-capital lines, related-party loans) and leases
assumptions._interestWhy: Built from the debt schedule (AR FY26 note 22; checked in MANKIND.ctx.js). NCDs: ₹1,250 cr at 7.99% repaid 16-Apr-2026 (15 days in FY27), ₹1,250 cr at 7.99% due 16-Oct-2026 (198 days), ₹2,500 cr at 7.97% due 16-Nov-2027 (full FY27, 229 days of FY28) = ₹258 / 125 / 0 cr; plus 7.5% on ₹1,204 cr of other borrowings (working-capital loans ₹639 cr, related-party loans ₹339 cr, term loans and accrued interest; held flat) = ₹90 cr; leases ~₹10 cr; other finance costs ~₹10 cr. Total ₹368 / 235 / 110 cr. Q1FY27 actual ₹110 cr (₹142 cr in Q4FY26) after the Apr-2026 repayment; FY26 ₹639 cr. We assume the NCDs are repaid from cash, not refinanced (management: acquisition debt repaid by FY28).
assumptions._taxWhy: Q1FY27 25.4% (25.5% per brokers): Mankind moved to the new tax regime (25.17%) in FY27 after the income-tax exemption on its Sikkim plant expired; FY26 was 16.9% and FY25 20.3%. The BSV amortisation is not tax-deductible, but the deferred tax liability created on the acquisition (₹1,800 cr) unwinds at 25.17% of it, so book tax stays near the statutory rate. This is the single biggest drag on FY27E EPS growth (~₹4.5 a share vs FY26's rate).
assumptions._payoutWhy: Mankind paid its first dividend in FY26: an interim ₹1 a share (₹41.27 cr, 2.2% of profit). Cash goes first to repaying the acquisition NCDs (₹1,250 cr in Apr-2026, ₹1,250 cr in Oct-2026, ₹2,500 cr in Nov-2027). We assume a 3% payout (₹1.7-2.4 a share).

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity: 6.5% + 0.8 x 6% = 11.3%. Net debt is ~3% of capital (₹3,377 cr at Jun-26 against a ~₹1.03 lakh cr market value) and falls to nil by FY28, so WACC ≈ cost of equity; beta 0.8 for a defensive, domestic-led pharma company.
dcf._tgWhy: 6% nominal: ~85% of revenue is India, where the branded market grows 8-10% a year in value.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~11% to 8% by year 15.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 27%: a little above the FY29E 26.8% as chronic and specialty mix rise, below the 28-29% of the best Indian branded peers (Abbott, Torrent's base).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: 4.5% of revenue: maintenance plus capacity for 8% growth after the Vadodara build (FY24-26: 3.8-5.2%).
dcf._depWhy: 3% of revenue = tax-deductible depreciation and amortisation only (book D&A FY27E ~5.8% of revenue, of which ~2.8pp is BSV acquisition amortisation that gives no tax saving).
